1: # Backend and shared API contract
2: 
3: Read PROJECT.md. These are proposed contract decisions to review before coding.
4: 
5: ## Architecture and data
6: 
7: Use TypeScript/Express, file-backed SQLite, migrations and parameterized queries. Separate HTTP handling, business rules and database access without unnecessary generic abstractions.
8: 
9: Vehicle fields: id (server-generated opaque string), make, model, category, price (integer paise), quantity (integer units). For example, price 125000000 means INR 1,250,000. Category initially accepts nonempty free text.
10: 
11: User fields include unique normalized email, password hash and server-controlled role. Never return hashes. Use a vetted password-hashing library, with configuration recorded during implementation.
12: 
13: ## Routes
14: 
15: All vehicle routes require Authorization: Bearer <token>. Check signature/expiry and trusted role; never accept body-supplied permissions.
16: 
17: | Route | Access | Request | Success |
18: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
19: | POST /api/auth/register | Public | email, password | 201 with user; log in separately |
20: | POST /api/auth/login | Public | email, password | 200 with token and user |
21: | POST /api/vehicles | Admin decision | make, model, category, price, quantity | 201 with vehicle |
22: | GET /api/vehicles | Authenticated | None | 200 with vehicles, including zero stock |
23: | GET /api/vehicles/search | Authenticated | Filters below | 200 with matches |
24: | PUT /api/vehicles/:id | Admin decision | Full make, model, category, price | 200 with updated vehicle |
25: | DELETE /api/vehicles/:id | Admin | None | 204 without body |
26: | POST /api/vehicles/:id/purchase | Authenticated | No body | 200 with vehicle after decrement by one |
27: | POST /api/vehicles/:id/restock | Admin | quantity: positive increment | 200 with updated vehicle |
28: 
29: Response envelopes: {vehicle: ...}, {vehicles: [...]}, {user: ...}, or login {token: "...", user: ...}. Returned user includes id, email, role.
30: 
31: Reject unknown mutation fields, including role on registration and quantity on PUT. This restriction on detail updates is a documented project decision.
32: 
33: Search parameters: make, model, category, minPrice, maxPrice. Price bounds are inclusive integer paise. Make/model: trimmed case-insensitive literal substring. Category: trimmed case-insensitive exact match. Combine with AND. No filters equals listing; ignore blank text filters. Reject malformed/repeated parameters and reversed bounds. Use stable ordering by id. Escape SQL LIKE wildcard characters to preserve literal matching.
34: 
35: ## Validation and errors
36: 
37: - Trim make/model/category; require 1-100 characters. Normalize email consistently before uniqueness checks. Syntax validation does not prove ownership.
38: - Proposed password length 12-128 characters; do not trim silently. Verify the chosen hashing library does not truncate accepted passwords. Generic invalid-credentials response.
39: - Price and creation quantity: nonnegative safe integers. Restock increment: positive safe integer. Reject fractional/negative values, numeric strings in JSON and overflow.
40: - Database constraints enforce required fields, unique email and nonnegative price/stock.
41: - 400 malformed JSON/validation; 401 missing/invalid/expired credentials; 403 forbidden; 404 missing vehicle; 409 duplicate email/insufficient stock; generic 500 unexpected error.
42: - Error shape: {"error":{"code":"OUT_OF_STOCK","message":"This vehicle is out of stock."}}. Field errors may be added for validation.
43: - No secrets, SQL errors or stack traces in responses. Authenticate/authorize before mutations.
44: - Configure body limits, explicit development origins, testable login abuse protection and environment-based secrets. Never log passwords/tokens or commit environment secrets. Fail clearly on missing required configuration.
45: - Initial logout clears the browser token. Refresh/revocation are outside core scope; do not claim them.
46: 
47: ## Inventory
48: 
49: Atomically decrement only while quantity is positive. A read followed by unconditional write is insufficient. Inspect affected rows, distinguish missing vehicle from zero stock safely, and atomically increment restock with overflow protection. Define busy/transaction handling for the actual driver; do not swallow database errors.
50: 
51: Test competing requests for the last unit with independent requests/connections where practical: one success, one stock conflict, final stock zero. Sequential tests alone are not concurrency evidence.
52: 
53: ## TDD evidence
54: 
55: Write/run a meaningful failing test, confirm intended failure, preserve Red commit, implement minimally, run tests and preserve Green. Refactor when useful. Missing imports/tools are not the intended business-rule failure. Tooling setup is not falsely labeled business TDD.
56: 
57: Use focused unit tests plus real HTTP/middleware/database integration. Cover invalid inputs, duplicate accounts, role escalation, expired tokens, forbidden operations, /search routing, wildcard handling, price bounds, missing IDs, stock limits and failed writes. Do not mock persistence in persistence tests.
58: 
59: Prove restart persistence by writing, closing the app/database, reopening the same file and reading the record. Record actual commands/results, never invented coverage or successes.

25: ## Screens
26: 
27: Authentication: focused labeled form, inline errors, accessible password visibility control, links between login/register. Optional modest desktop brand panel disappears on phones. Preserve nonsecret inputs after recoverable errors.
28: 
29: Inventory header: CarDeal IS, Inventory, admin-only Manage, account identity and logout. Title Vehicle inventory and result count from actual data.
30: 
31: Wide layout: approximately 260 px filter sidebar plus flexible card grid. Medium: two columns where they fit. Phone: one column with expandable filters. Support 360 px without horizontal scrolling, at least 16 px outer padding; 24-32 px on desktop.
32: 
33: Cards: make/model, category, INR price, quantity/stock label, Purchase button. Optional 16:10 image area with polished fallback. Align actions without truncating important information. Document asset rights and use suitable alt text.
34: 
35: Filters: make, model, category, min/max price, Apply filters and Clear filters. Category text field is acceptable until a complete category source exists. Show rupees; convert precisely to integer paise. Reject malformed currency rather than silently rounding. Explicit Apply avoids excessive keystroke requests.
36: 
37: Admin: Add, Edit, Delete and Restock. Desktop table can become phone cards. Consistent reusable forms. Edit excludes quantity. Restock requests an integer increment. Delete confirmation names the vehicle. Hide admin controls from regular users; backend authorization remains mandatory.
38: 
39: ## States
40: 
41: | State | Behavior |
42: | --- | --- |
43: | Loading | Stable skeleton/progress, no fake records |
44: | Empty inventory | Explanation and admin add action |
45: | No matches | Active filters and clear action |
46: | Request failure | Useful error and safe retry |
47: | Zero stock | Label and disabled Purchase |
48: | Purchase pending | Disable that button, prevent duplicate submission |
49: | Purchase success | Use returned stock and accessible announcement |
50: | Stock conflict | Explain and refresh inventory |
51: | Uncertain purchase network outcome | Refresh; never automatically repeat purchase |
52: | Expired session | Clear session and explain login redirect |
53: | Forbidden | Explain restriction, never fake success |
54: | Invalid input | Field-linked errors and focus first invalid field |

56: Never report success before the API confirms it. Prevent stale search responses overwriting newer results. Finished screens use real API data; fixtures remain isolated to tests.

65: 
66: Small typed API client, reusable forms/cards and focused pages. Add global state libraries only when justified. Initial bearer token lives in memory; reload requires login. This is a documented tradeoff, not persistent-session support. Do not silently change storage/auth design.

    $stream.Close()

    # Split by paragraph <w:p>
    $paras = [regex]::Split($content, '</w:p>')
    $paraTexts = foreach ($p in $paras) {
        $matches = [regex]::Matches($p, '<w:t[^>]*>(.*?)</w:t>')
        $line = ($matches | ForEach-Object { $_.Groups[1].Value }) -join ''
        if ($line.Trim().Length -gt 0) { $line }
    }
    $paraTexts -join "`n" | Out-File -FilePath $outTxtPath -Encoding utf8

## 2. Specification Comparison: Original Assignment vs. Proposed Guides

A rigorous line-by-line comparison between the original Round 1 assignment (`AI_Kata_Car_Dealership_Inventory_System_V2.docx`), the JD (`SCInternJD1 (1).docx`), and the repository guides (`PROJECT.md`, `BACKEND.md`, `FRONTEND.md`, `WORKFLOW.md`, `README.md`, `PROMPTS.md`) reveals the following distinctions:

### A. Omissions and De-prioritizations
1. **Live Deployment**: The Kata notes live deployment on Vercel/Netlify/Heroku/AWS as optional ("Brownie Points"). The guides appropriately de-prioritize deployment to focus strictly on local craftsmanship, TDD rigor, and reproducible test suites.
2. **Java Context in JD**: The JD lists Java among desired proficiencies. `PROJECT.md` explicitly notes that Java is not an approved backend option for this Kata (which restricts backend choices to Node.js/TypeScript, Python, or Ruby).
3. **Images**: The Kata makes no mention of car image URLs or asset management. `PROJECT.md` and `FRONTEND.md` treat car images as optional with a designed fallback, keeping core focus on inventory and transaction logic.

### B. Contradictions and Harmonizations
1. **Admin Permissions on Vehicle Mutations**:
   - *Kata Endpoint List*: Lists `POST /api/vehicles` (Add) and `PUT /api/vehicles/:id` (Update) under "Vehicles (Protected)" alongside `GET`, while explicitly marking only `DELETE /api/vehicles/:id` and `POST /api/vehicles/:id/restock` as "(Admin only)".
   - *Kata Frontend Section*: Contrarily specifies "(For Admin Users) Forms/UI to add, update, and delete vehicles".
   - *Guides' Choice*: `PROJECT.md` and `BACKEND.md` harmonize this contradiction by making vehicle creation (`POST`) and update (`PUT`) **Admin-only** in the backend API as well. This prevents standard authenticated users from bypassing the UI to mutate inventory data.
2. **Quantity Edits on PUT**:
   - *Kata*: States `PUT /api/vehicles/:id : Update a vehicle's details` without field restrictions.
   - *Guides*: `BACKEND.md` explicitly forbids updating `quantity` via `PUT`, requiring stock to change strictly through `/purchase` and `/restock`. This prevents race conditions and un-audited inventory overrides.

### C. Material Proposed Choices (Not Mandated by Recruiter)
1. **Currency and Price Representation**: The Kata mentions only "price". The guides propose Indian Rupees (**INR**) stored and transferred as integer **paise** (1 INR = 100 paise; e.g., ₹12,50,000 = `125000000`).
2. **Purchase Quantity**: The Kata specifies decreasing quantity. The guides specify exactly **1 unit per request** with no request body accepted.
3. **Restock Semantics**: The Kata specifies increasing quantity. The guides define restock as a positive additive increment (`{ quantity: <positive integer> }`), not an absolute overwrite.
4. **Search Semantics**: The Kata states "Search for vehicles by make, model, category, or price range." The guides define all filters as combining via `AND`, using case-insensitive substring matching for `make` and `model`, exact case-insensitive match for `category`, and inclusive bounds for `minPrice` and `maxPrice`.
5. **Session Persistence**: In-memory token storage (page refresh returns user to login) rather than `localStorage` or refresh-token cookies.
6. **Admin Provisioning**: No public registration role selector or hardcoded seeds; admin is provisioned via an isolated CLI command script.

Hidden from regular users. | **Agreed.** Regular users cannot create or modify inventory either via UI or direct API calls. |
| **PUT Quantity Restriction** | Rejects `quantity` field in PUT payload with `400 Bad Request`. | Edit form explicitly omits quantity field. | **Agreed.** Prevents arbitrary inventory alterations. Prevents race conditions with active buyers. |
| **1-Unit Purchases** | `POST /api/vehicles/:id/purchase` takes no body; decrements stock by exactly 1 unit atomically. | "Purchase" button fires request without quantity picker. | **Agreed.** Bulk ordering is out of scope. Every purchase transaction is exactly 1 vehicle. |

Before proceeding to Stage 1, please review and confirm the following 5 proposed design choices:

1. **Admin Authorization for Vehicle Add/Update**:
   - *Proposal*: Restrict `POST /api/vehicles` and `PUT /api/vehicles/:id` to `role: "admin"`.

2. **SQLite Driver Mechanism**:
   - *Proposal*: Leverage Node 26's built-in `node:sqlite` module for zero-dependency native SQLite operations, or alternatively install `better-sqlite3` (pending Windows N-API build checks).
3. **Category Field Constraints**:
   - *Proposal*: Free-text string (1-100 characters) normalized and trimmed, matching search by case-insensitive exact match.
   - *Alternative*: Strict enumeration (e.g., `Sedan`, `SUV`, `Hatchback`, `Truck`, `Coupe`, `Electric`).
4. **Session Storage Mechanism**:
   - *Proposal*: In-memory token storage (page refresh requires re-login, highest security, zero XSS token exposure).

5. **Currency Unit & Precision**:

args.Content:
# CarDeal IS

A full-stack Car Dealership Inventory System for Incubyte Round 1.

**Status: Backend Complete & Fully Tested (Consolidated Stage 1). Frontend implementation pending (Stage 2).**

## Functionality Overview

- **Authentication & Authorization**: User registration with scrypt password hashing, login with signed JWT issuance, and server-side role enforcement (`user` vs. `admin`).
- **Vehicle Catalog**: Protected vehicle listing including zero-stock visibility with out-of-stock indicators.
- **Search & Filtering**: Multi-parameter search by make (case-insensitive substring), model (case-insensitive substring), category (case-insensitive exact match), and inclusive integer paise price bounds with SQL wildcard sanitization.
- **Atomic Transactions & Inventory**: Single-unit purchases with atomic stock decrement (`WHERE quantity > 0`) preventing negative inventory under concurrency. Admin-only additive restock increments with positive integer validation.
- **Persistent Storage**: Persistent file-backed SQLite database with automated migration application on startup.

## Technology Stack

- **Backend**: Node.js (`v26.7.0`), TypeScript (`5.7.2`), Express (`4.21.2`)
- **Database**: File-backed SQLite utilizing Node.js built-in `node:sqlite` (`DatabaseSync` with WAL journal mode)
- **Security & Tokens**: Node built-in `crypto.scrypt` (salt + timing-safe equality), `jsonwebtoken` (`9.0.2`)
- **Testing**: `vitest` (`2.1.8`), `supertest` (`7.0.0`)
- **Frontend (Pending Stage 2)**: React, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS with Vite

## Guides & Specifications

- [Requirements and Decisions](PROJECT.md)
- [Backend and Shared API Contract](BACKEND.md)
- [Frontend Design and Visual States](FRONTEND.md)
- [Development and Review Workflow](WORKFLOW.md)
- [AI Conversation Records](PROMPTS.md)

## Verified Local Backend Setup

### Prerequisites
- Node.js `v22.x` or `v26.x` (verified with `v26.7.0` using built-in `node:sqlite`)
- npm `11.x`+

### 1. Installation
From the repository root:
```bash
cd backend
npm install
```

### 2. Environment Configuration
Create a `.env` file in `backend/` (or copy from `backend/.env.example`):
```bash
PORT=4000
DATABASE_PATH=./data/cardeal.db
JWT_SECRET=cardeal_secure_dev_jwt_secret_key_at_least_32_chars!
JWT_EXPIRES_IN=24h
CORS_ORIGIN=http://localhost:5173
```

### 3. Local Administrator Provisioning
Provision an administrator account locally without public role selectors or default passwords:
```bash
# From backend directory:
npm run admin:provision <email> <password>

# Example:
npm run admin:provision admin@cardeal.com AdminPassword123!
```

### 4. Running the Backend Server
```bash
# Development mode (auto-reload via tsx):
npm run dev

# Or compile and start production build:
npm run build
npm start
```
The API server will listen on `http://localhost:4000`.

## Verified Tests & Test Suite Execution

All 29 integration and domain tests run against isolated temporary SQLite files and clean up automatically.

To execute the test suite:
```bash
# From backend directory:
npm test

# From repository root:
npm run test:backend
```

### Test Suite Summary
- `tests/canary.test.ts`: Infrastructure and TypeScript execution verification.
- `tests/auth_registration.test.ts`: User registration persistence in SQLite with scrypt password hash verification against correct and incorrect passwords.
- `tests/auth_validation.test.ts`: Email regex, password length bounds (12-128 chars), 409 duplicate email conflicts, and role escalation prevention.
- `tests/auth_login.test.ts`: Login credential verification, JWT token issuance with expiration, and generic 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS.
- `tests/auth_middleware_and_admin.test.ts`: Bearer token authentication middleware, 401 UNAUTHORIZED/INVALID_TOKEN, 403 FORBIDDEN enforcement, and admin provisioning CLI.
- `tests/vehicles_crud.test.ts`: Admin vehicle creation with integer paise price validation, zero-stock catalog listing, PUT detail update with quantity modification rejection, and admin deletion.
- `tests/vehicles_search.test.ts`: Case-insensitive substring make/model search, exact category filter, inclusive paise bounds, reversed bounds rejection (400), and SQL LIKE wildcard escaping (`%` and `_`).
- `tests/purchase_and_restock.test.ts`: Atomic 1-unit purchase, 409 OUT_OF_STOCK handling, competing concurrent requests for the final unit (exactly 1 succeeds, 1 gets 409 conflict, final stock 0), and admin additive restock.
- `tests/database_restart_persistence.test.ts`: Full application and database restart verification proving persisted records, hashes, and inventory changes survive process shutdown and database reopening.

## Frontend Application

*Status: Pending Stage 2 implementation (Target: 9:25 PM IST).*

## Screenshots

## My AI Usage

### Tools and Actual Use
- **ChatGPT**: Assisted with interpreting the assignment and JD, structuring the initial guides, and planning test cases.
- **Antigravity with Gemini 3.8 Flash**: Executed repository inspection, verified `node:sqlite` compatibility on Node 26, drove genuine Red-Green-Refactor TDD slices, implemented database schema/migrations, services, controllers, routes, CLI provisioning, and restart persistence tests.

## 4. Issues Encountered, Root Cause & How Fixed

1. **Vite Bundle Interception of Built-in `node:sqlite`**:
   - *Issue*: During Vitest startup, Vite attempted to load `node:sqlite` as an external npm package `sqlite`, throwing `Failed to load url sqlite (resolved id: sqlite)`.
   - *How Found*: Running initial test execution on Slice 1.
   - *Fix*: Created a dedicated `nodeRequire` helper using `createRequire(import.meta.url)` in `backend/src/database/connection.ts` to bypass Vite's module bundler and directly resolve Node 26's native built-in `node:sqlite`.
2. **TypeScript CommonJS vs. ESM Mismatch**:
   - *Issue*: `tsc` failed with `TS1470: The 'import.meta' meta-property is not allowed in files which will build into CommonJS output` and `TS2441: Duplicate identifier 'require'`.
   - *How Found*: Running `npm run build` after implementing `server.ts`.
   - *Fix*: Added `"type": "module"` to `backend/package.json` and renamed the internal loader to `nodeRequire`. TypeScript compiled cleanly with 0 errors.

thinking:
Explicit configuration of the JWT secret is critical for security, eliminating reliance on any default values or fallbacks within the code. The minimum length requirement ensures a strong secret, preventing brute-force attacks. Removed fallback strings from the authentication service.


Implemented a critical check in the application's startup to ensure the JWT secret is defined, failing fast if missing to prevent security vulnerabilities. Enhanced JWT expiration handling to respect environment variables or configuration options for flexible token lifetimes. Updated the example configuration file with instructions on generating strong secrets.

Added robust input validation across the application to handle potential integer overflows and invalid input values. Implemented checks to ensure that restock increments do not exceed safe integer limits and that search price ranges are valid. This prevents unexpected behavior or errors related to exceeding numerical boundaries.


To handle duplicate registrations, the registration function now includes a try-catch block around the database insertion. The error handler specifically checks for "UNIQUE constraint failed" messages, returning a 409 error with a "DUPLICATE_EMAIL" code if the email is already in use; otherwise, it re-throws the original error.

Implemented global error handling middleware in the application to provide consistent error responses. This middleware standardizes error codes and messages, returning a 500 error with "INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR" for unexpected exceptions and a generic "ERROR" code otherwise.

The admin provisioning script now loads environment variables, allowing the `DATABASE_PATH` to be configured via the environment. This change supports flexible database path specification, falling back to a default if the variable is not set.


Defined allowed keys for vehicle creation and update, rejecting requests with unexpected fields to improve input validation. Implemented logic to reject request bodies for the purchase endpoint, and to reject unknown or array-based query parameters within search functionality. Added registration validation to reject unknown fields.

Implemented login abuse protection middleware to track failed login attempts by key and block after a threshold, returning a "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS" error. The counter is reset on successful login. Exported a reset function for easier testing.

Focusing on the `vehicleService.ts` file, the plan is to enhance data integrity. Implementing safe integer checks will be critical throughout the service to prevent unexpected behavior. Also, unknown fields in `create` and `update` calls will be rejected to improve data validation.

Further validation is necessary for the search query and the purchase body to maintain data integrity. The search query validation must reject unknown query parameters, and array parameters while enforcing safe integer bounds. Also, the purchase body, if present, should be rejected.

Explicitly configure the JWT secret and ensure it meets a minimum length requirement, prioritizing explicitly provided options or environment variables. Pass JWT expiration time to the authentication service, defaulting to 24 hours if no specific value is provided. Enhance the error handler to sanitize internal server error messages, preventing the leakage of sensitive information like SQL queries or stack traces.

AuthContext will manage the in-memory token, user data (ID, email, role), and a session expiry message. It will also provide methods for login, registration, and logout. A key function will be wiring up a callback to handle unauthorized responses (401), clearing the token and setting the session expiry message accordingly.

Planning the UI components, starting with `Navbar.tsx` which will contain the header, user information, and management controls. The `AuthModal.tsx` component is next, focusing on accessible login and registration forms, including email input.


Considering `AuthModal.tsx` details, the login form requires a password field with visibility toggle and inline error messages, and will preserve email on recoverable errors. The vehicle card (`VehicleCard.tsx`) design includes make/model header, category pill, price, stock status, purchase button (disabled under certain conditions), and admin actions. The filtering sidebar (`FilterSidebar.tsx`) implementation will handle responsive filter inputs for vehicle attributes, with apply and clear buttons. The admin modal (`AdminModal.tsx`) needs components for adding and editing vehicle details, but the edit will exclude initial quantity.

Identifying required features for the authentication view component: tabbed interface for sign-in/create account, inline error display, email persistence across form states, password visibility toggle, and informative notice regarding in-memory authentication. These will guide the implementation of the component's functionality.

Considering the `FilterSidebar` component, need to implement filter fields for `make`, `model`, `category`, `minRupees`, and `maxRupees`, along with "Apply filters" and "Clear filters" actions. The component must be responsive, featuring a static desktop sidebar and a collapsible mobile view optimized for a `360px` width. Accessibility, including labels, inputs, and keyboard navigation, is a key requirement.

Planning the `VehicleCard` component structure. The card will display vehicle make/model, category, and formatted price. Stock availability will be indicated with a badge showing either quantity or "Out of Stock". A "Purchase" button will be included, disabled when the vehicle is out of stock or during purchasing to prevent multiple clicks.

Determining the required form fields for the admin modal based on its operational mode ("add," "edit," "restock"). The "add" mode requires fields for make, model, category, price, and initial quantity. "Edit" mode will include make, model, category, and price, explicitly excluding quantity, which is managed through other actions. "Restock" mode presents a named modal, displaying the current stock level.

The application's top-level structure in `App.tsx` will conditionally render based on authentication status. When unauthenticated, the component displays an `AuthView`. Conversely, authenticated users see a `Navbar` with user information, administrative toggles, and logout, alongside the core content in a styled container. The main content will contain a title "Vehicle Inventory" and a subtitle indicating the number of vehicles.

Planning frontend behavior tests for key components. Focusing on `VehicleCard.test.tsx`, aiming to verify the rendering of vehicle details including the price format. Need to ensure the "Purchase" button is disabled and displays "Out of Stock" when stock is zero, and that a spinner appears with the disabled button during the purchasing state.

args.Content:
# CarDeal IS

A modern, full-stack Car Dealership Inventory System for Incubyte Round 1. Built with a Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflow, strict software craftsmanship practices, and transparent AI pairing.

## Planned vs. Implemented Functionality

- **User Authentication**: Token-based authentication using signed JWTs. Passwords hashed using non-truncating `scrypt` with salt and constant-time equality checks.
- **Role-Based Access**: Public registration defaults strictly to standard buyer privileges. Admin capabilities are managed server-side and provisioned via a dedicated local CLI tool.
- **Vehicle Catalog**: Protected browsing of inventory with stock quantity tracking, including zero-stock visibility.
- **Search & Filtering**: Multi-parameter search by make (case-insensitive substring), model (case-insensitive substring), category (case-insensitive exact match), and inclusive integer paise price bounds with SQL wildcard sanitization.
- **Atomic Transactions & Inventory**: Single-unit purchases with atomic stock decrement (`WHERE quantity > 0`) preventing negative inventory under concurrency. Admin-only additive restock increments with safe-integer validation.
- **Frontend SPA**: Original React, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, and Tailwind CSS user interface adhering to agreed visual tokens and responsive layouts.

## Architecture & Technology Stack

- **Backend API**: Node.js (`v26.7.0`), Express (`4.21.2`), TypeScript (`5.7.2`)
- **Database**: File-backed SQLite utilizing Node.js native built-in `node:sqlite` (`DatabaseSync` with WAL journal mode)
- **Security & Tokens**: Node built-in `crypto.scrypt`, `jsonwebtoken` (`9.0.2`) with brute-force rate limiting (`429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`)
- **Testing**: `vitest` (`2.1.8`), `supertest` (`7.0.0`), `@testing-library/react` (`16.1.0`), `@testing-library/jest-dom` (`6.6.3`)
- **Frontend SPA**: React (`18.3.1`), Vite (`5.4.11`), Tailwind CSS (`3.4.17`)

---

## Local Setup & Execution Guide

### Prerequisites
- **Node.js**: `v22.x` or `v26.x` (verified with `v26.7.0`, requiring built-in `node:sqlite`)
- **npm**: `11.x`+

### 1. Installation
Install dependencies for both backend and frontend from the repository root:
```bash
# Install backend packages
npm --prefix backend install

# Install frontend packages
npm --prefix frontend install
```

### 2. Environment Configuration
Create a `.env` file inside `backend/` (or copy from `backend/.env.example`):
```env
PORT=4000
DATABASE_PATH=./data/cardeal.db
# Generate a secure private key (e.g., openssl rand -hex 32)
JWT_SECRET=replace_with_a_secure_private_secret_at_least_32_characters_long
JWT_EXPIRES_IN=24h
CORS_ORIGIN=http://localhost:5173
```
*Note: The backend enforces that `JWT_SECRET` must be explicitly configured and at least 32 characters long; it will refuse to start with missing or fallback secrets.*

### 3. Local Administrator Provisioning
Provision an initial administrator account locally without exposing public role selectors or default passwords:
```bash
# From repository root:
npm run admin:provision admin@cardeal.com AdminPassword123!

# Or from backend directory:
npm --prefix backend run admin:provision admin@cardeal.com AdminPassword123!
```

### 4. Running the Complete Application

#### Start the Backend API (Port 4000)
```bash
# Development mode (auto-reload via tsx):
npm run dev:backend

# Or build and run production:
npm run build:backend
npm --prefix backend start
```

#### Start the Frontend SPA (Port 5173)
```bash
# In a separate terminal:
npm run dev:frontend
```
Open your browser to `http://localhost:5173`.

---

## Running the Test Suites

Both backend and frontend feature automated test suites running on Vitest.

### Run All Tests (Root)
```bash
npm test
```

### Run Backend Tests Separately (37 Tests in 11 Suites)
```bash
npm run test:backend
```
Backend coverage includes:
- `canary.test.ts`: Tooling and TypeScript runtime verification.
- `auth_registration.test.ts`: User registration persistence in SQLite with scrypt password verification.
- `auth_validation.test.ts`: Email regex, password length bounds (12–128 chars), 409 duplicate email conflicts, and role escalation prevention.
- `auth_login.test.ts`: Credential verification, JWT issuance with expiration, and generic 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS.
- `auth_middleware_and_admin.test.ts`: Bearer token authentication, 401/403 status enforcement, and admin CLI provisioning.
- `vehicles_crud.test.ts`: Admin vehicle creation, integer paise price validation, zero-stock catalog listing, PUT detail update with quantity modification rejection, and admin deletion.
- `vehicles_search.test.ts`: Substring make/model search, exact category filter, inclusive paise bounds, reversed bounds rejection (400), and SQL `LIKE` wildcard escaping.
- `purchase_and_restock.test.ts`: Atomic 1-unit purchase, 409 OUT_OF_STOCK handling, concurrent competing requests for the final unit (exactly 1 succeeds, 1 gets 409 conflict, final stock 0), and admin additive restock.
- `database_restart_persistence.test.ts`: Verifies records, hashes, and inventory changes survive process shutdown and database reopening.
- `regression_fixes.test.ts`: Regression suite verifying explicit secret enforcement, expired tokens, brute-force throttling, safe-integer boundaries, concurrent duplicate registration, and strict mutation payloads.
- `e2e_integration_flow.test.ts`: End-to-end multi-step integration test validating the complete business flow.

### Run Frontend Tests Separately (11 Tests in 3 Suites)
```bash
npm run test:frontend
```
Frontend coverage includes:
- `currency.test.ts`: Precise rupee-to-paise conversion, rejection of malformed currency and fractional paise, and Indian currency formatting (`₹`).
- `VehicleCard.test.tsx`: Card rendering, price formatting, zero-stock disablement, in-flight spinner state, and admin controls.
- `App.test.tsx`: Authentication view rendering and form validation.

---

## Screenshots

Actual screenshots captured from the live application using headless Chrome across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports:

### Desktop (1440px Viewport)
![Desktop View](docs/screenshots/desktop_1440.png)

### Tablet (768px Viewport)
![Tablet View](docs/screenshots/tablet_768.png)

### Mobile (360px Viewport)
![Mobile View](docs/screenshots/mobile_360.png)

---

## Known Design Trade-offs & Current Limitations

1. **In-Memory Session Storage**: As specified in the architecture agreement, the client stores JWT bearer tokens in memory to eliminate local storage vulnerabilities. Refreshing or reloading the browser clears the session and requires re-authenticating.
2. **Node.js Runtime Requirement**: The backend utilizes Node.js native `node:sqlite`, which requires Node.js `v22.x` or `v26.x`.
3. **Currency Precision**: All prices are stored and communicated via the API as non-negative integer paise to eliminate floating-point rounding errors.

---

## My AI Usage

### Tools and Actual Use
- **ChatGPT**: Used for initial interpretation of the kata requirements, drafting architectural guidelines, and outlining the TDD strategy.
- **Antigravity with Gemini 3.8 Flash**: Served as the interactive coding partner. Executed directory and tooling inspections, verified `node:sqlite` compatibility, drove Red-Green-Refactor test cycles for both backend and frontend, implemented services, controllers, routes, CLI tools, React components, and captured multi-viewport screenshots.

### Reflection
*The candidate's personal reflection will be added in their own voice prior to final submission.*

### Conversation Transparency
Full unedited chat logs and transcripts are preserved in [PROMPTS.md](PROMPTS.md).

## 1. Summary of Independently Reviewed Backend Issues & Regression Fixes

Every defect was reproduced first with an intentional failing regression assertion (`commit e469379 (red)`), followed by the minimal architectural fix (`commit 18eb25f (green)`):

| # | Reviewed Defect | Failing Test Evidence (Red) | Resolution & Architectural Fix (Green) |
| :- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | **Fallback JWT signing secret allowed startup without secret** | `expect(() => createApp({ dbManager })).toThrow(/JWT secret must be explicitly configured/)` failed because hardcoded default secret permitted startup. | Removed fallback secret literals from `app.ts`, `server.ts`, `authService.ts`, and `authMiddleware.ts`. Made `JWT_SECRET` mandatory (≥ 32 chars). Injected test-only secrets in test suites. Honored `JWT_EXPIRES_IN`. |
| **2** | **Prices, quantities, and search bounds lacked safe-integer constraints** | Test sending `price: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 1000` returned `201 Created`; restock overflow test allowed corrupting stored stock. | Enforced `Number.isSafeInteger(val)` and non-negativity across vehicle create, update, and search bounds. Added safe integer boundary checks in `restock` ensuring `current.quantity + increment <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. |
| **3** | **Concurrent duplicate registration triggered 500 error** | Concurrent registration test `Promise.all([reg1, reg2])` returned `[201, 500]` due to unhandled SQLite `UNIQUE constraint failed: users.email`. | Wrapped SQLite insert in a try/catch block mapping `UNIQUE constraint failed` to a clean `409 Conflict` with `code: "DUPLICATE_EMAIL"`, guaranteeing exactly 1 user persisted. |
| **4** | **Database/internal details leaked in unexpected 500 errors** | Unhandled database rejections returned raw error messages and internal SQL details to callers. | Updated centralized error-handling middleware in `app.ts` to sanitize all 500-level responses to a generic, opaque payload: `{"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR","message":"An unexpected error occurred."}}`. |
| **5** | **Admin CLI did not load environment config or custom `DATABASE_PATH`** | Admin CLI relied on fallback defaults and did not load `.env` variables or custom paths. | Added `dotenv.config()` to `provisionAdmin.ts` and configured it to dynamically resolve `process.env.DATABASE_PATH`. Verified execution against custom database files. |
| **6** | **Mutation endpoints accepted unknown fields and unexpected bodies** | `POST /api/vehicles` accepted extra injected fields; `POST /api/vehicles/:id/purchase` accepted request bodies despite contract specifying no body; `/search` accepted repeated array params. | Enforced strict key whitelisting on vehicle mutations; rejected extra fields with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; rejected request bodies on `/purchase` with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; rejected array/repeated query parameters and unknown filters on `/search`. |
| **+** | **Expired tokens & login abuse protection** | Expired tokens were untested; brute-force login attacks were unthrottled. | Added test rejecting expired tokens with `401 INVALID_TOKEN`. Added testable brute-force protection (`rateLimiter.ts`) returning `429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` after 5 consecutive failed login attempts. |

---

## 2. Completed Frontend Application Flows

Built an original Single Page Application in `frontend/` using **React 18**, **TypeScript**, **Tailwind CSS**, and **Vite** without copying any React Bits components or prebuilt templates:

1. **Authentication Flow (`AuthView.tsx` & `AuthContext.tsx`)**:
   - Tabbed interface switching seamlessly between Sign In and Registration.
   - Inline field-level error messages with accessible `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` links.
   - Password character visibility toggle ("Show" / "Hide") with accessible labels.
   - In-memory bearer token storage: token lives solely in application state. Reloading requires logging in again (honestly explained in UI notice).
   - Automatic 401 interception: clears expired session and displays explanatory notification.
2. **Vehicle Catalog & Responsive Layout (`App.tsx`, `Navbar.tsx`, `VehicleCard.tsx`)**:
   - Header displaying brand identity, user email, role pill (`Administrator` / `Standard Buyer`), and Sign Out.
   - Clean color palette adhering to agreed tokens: `#F6F7F5` page, `#FFFFFF` cards, `#172126` charcoal typography, `#0F766E` restrained teal accent, `#DCE3E1` borders, `#B42318` errors.
   - Indian Rupee currency formatting (`₹25,00,000`) derived accurately from integer paise.
   - Out-of-stock badge when `quantity === 0`, accompanied by disabled Purchase button.
   - In-flight purchase spinner preventing duplicate double-clicks.
   - Stock conflict handling: if a competing buyer takes the last unit, displays a 409 conflict notice and automatically refreshes inventory.
3. **Search & Filter Sidebar (`FilterSidebar.tsx`)**:
   - Inputs for Make, Model, Category, Min Price (₹), Max Price (₹).
   - Explicit "Apply Filters" button preventing search race conditions on rapid typing.
   - Stale response prevention: increments request identifiers so late-arriving responses cannot overwrite newer search results.
   - Collapsible mobile drawer for 360px viewports; static 260px sidebar for desktop.
4. **Administrator Management Flow (`AdminModal.tsx`)**:
   - Accessible modal supporting Add, Edit, Restock, and Delete.
   - Add Vehicle: make, model, category, rupee price, initial stock units.
   - Edit Vehicle: make, model, category, rupee price (**explicitly excludes quantity field** per specification).
   - Restock Vehicle: displays current stock and takes an integer increment (+units).
   - Delete Confirmation: explicitly names the vehicle before confirming deletion (`Are you sure you want to delete Toyota Camry?`).
   - Closes on `Escape` key and backdrop click.

1: # CarDeal IS
2: 
3: A modern, full-stack Car Dealership Inventory System for Incubyte Round 1. Built with a Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflow, strict software craftsmanship practices, and transparent AI pairing.
4: 
5: ## Planned vs. Implemented Functionality
6: 
7: - **User Authentication**: Token-based authentication using signed JWTs. Passwords hashed using non-truncating `scrypt` with salt and constant-time equality checks.
8: - **Role-Based Access**: Public registration defaults strictly to standard buyer privileges. Admin capabilities are managed server-side and provisioned via a dedicated local CLI tool.
9: - **Vehicle Catalog**: Protected browsing of inventory with stock quantity tracking, including zero-stock visibility.
10: - **Search & Filtering**: Multi-parameter search by make (case-insensitive substring), model (case-insensitive substring), category (case-insensitive exact match), and inclusive integer paise price bounds with SQL wildcard sanitization.
11: - **Atomic Transactions & Inventory**: Single-unit purchases with atomic stock decrement (`WHERE quantity > 0`) preventing negative inventory under concurrency. Admin-only additive restock increments with safe-integer validation.
12: - **Frontend SPA**: Original React, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, and Tailwind CSS user interface adhering to agreed visual tokens and responsive layouts.
13: 
14: ## Architecture & Technology Stack
15: 
16: - **Backend API**: Node.js (`v26.7.0`), Express (`4.21.2`), TypeScript (`5.7.2`)
17: - **Database**: File-backed SQLite utilizing Node.js native built-in `node:sqlite` (`DatabaseSync` with WAL journal mode)
18: - **Security & Tokens**: Node built-in `crypto.scrypt`, `jsonwebtoken` (`9.0.2`) with brute-force rate limiting (`429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`)
19: - **Testing**: `vitest` (`2.1.8`), `supertest` (`7.0.0`), `@testing-library/react` (`16.1.0`), `@testing-library/jest-dom` (`6.6.3`)
20: - **Frontend SPA**: React (`18.3.1`), Vite (`5.4.11`), Tailwind CSS (`3.4.17`)
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## Local Setup & Execution Guide
25: 
26: ### Prerequisites
27: - **Node.js**: `v22.x` or `v26.x` (verified with `v26.7.0`, requiring built-in `node:sqlite`)
28: - **npm**: `11.x`+
29: 
30: ### 1. Installation
31: Install dependencies for both backend and frontend from the repository root:
32: ```bash
33: # Install backend packages
34: npm --prefix backend install
35: 
36: # Install frontend packages
37: npm --prefix frontend install
38: ```
39: 
40: ### 2. Environment Configuration
41: Create a `.env` file inside `backend/` (or copy from `backend/.env.example`):
42: ```env
43: PORT=4000
44: DATABASE_PATH=./data/cardeal.db
45: # Generate a secure private key (e.g., openssl rand -hex 32)
46: JWT_SECRET=replace_with_a_secure_private_secret_at_least_32_characters_long
47: JWT_EXPIRES_IN=24h
48: CORS_ORIGIN=http://localhost:5173
49: ```
50: *Note: The backend enforces that `JWT_SECRET` must be explicitly configured and at least 32 characters long; it will refuse to start with missing or fallback secrets.*
51: 
52: ### 3. Local Administrator Provisioning
53: Provision an initial administrator account locally without exposing public role selectors or default passwords:
54: ```bash
55: # From repository root:
56: npm run admin:provision admin@cardeal.com AdminPassword123!
57: 
58: # Or from backend directory:
59: npm --prefix backend run admin:provision admin@cardeal.com AdminPassword123!
60: ```
61: 
62: ### 4. Running the Complete Application
63: 
64: #### Start the Backend API (Port 4000)
65: ```bash
66: # Development mode (auto-reload via tsx):
67: npm run dev:backend
68: 
69: # Or build and run production:
70: npm run build:backend
71: npm --prefix backend start
72: ```
73: 
74: #### Start the Frontend SPA (Port 5173)
75: ```bash
76: # In a separate terminal:
77: npm run dev:frontend
78: ```
79: Open your browser to `http://localhost:5173`.
80: 
81: ---
82: 
83: ## Running the Test Suites
84: 
85: Both backend and frontend feature automated test suites running on Vitest.
86: 
87: ### Run All Tests (Root)
88: ```bash
89: npm test
90: ```
91: 
92: ### Run Backend Tests Separately (37 Tests in 11 Suites)
93: ```bash
94: npm run test:backend
95: ```
96: Backend coverage includes:
97: - `canary.test.ts`: Tooling and TypeScript runtime verification.
98: - `auth_registration.test.ts`: User registration persistence in SQLite with scrypt password verification.
99: - `auth_validation.test.ts`: Email regex, password length bounds (12–128 chars), 409 duplicate email conflicts, and role escalation prevention.
100: - `auth_login.test.ts`: Credential verification, JWT issuance with expiration, and generic 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS.

101: - `auth_middleware_and_admin.test.ts`: Bearer token authentication, 401/403 status enforcement, and admin CLI provisioning.
102: - `vehicles_crud.test.ts`: Admin vehicle creation, integer paise price validation, zero-stock catalog listing, PUT detail update with quantity modification rejection, and admin deletion.
103: - `vehicles_search.test.ts`: Substring make/model search, exact category filter, inclusive paise bounds, reversed bounds rejection (400), and SQL `LIKE` wildcard escaping.
104: - `purchase_and_restock.test.ts`: Atomic 1-unit purchase, 409 OUT_OF_STOCK handling, concurrent competing requests for the final unit (exactly 1 succeeds, 1 gets 409 conflict, final stock 0), and admin additive restock.
105: - `database_restart_persistence.test.ts`: Verifies records, hashes, and inventory changes survive process shutdown and database reopening.
106: - `regression_fixes.test.ts`: Regression suite verifying explicit secret enforcement, expired tokens, brute-force throttling, safe-integer boundaries, concurrent duplicate registration, and strict mutation payloads.
107: - `e2e_integration_flow.test.ts`: End-to-end multi-step integration test validating the complete business flow.
108: 
109: ### Run Frontend Tests Separately (11 Tests in 3 Suites)

111: npm run test:frontend
112: ```
113: Frontend coverage includes:
114: - `currency.test.ts`: Precise rupee-to-paise conversion, rejection of malformed currency and fractional paise, and Indian currency formatting (`₹`).
115: - `VehicleCard.test.tsx`: Card rendering, price formatting, zero-stock disablement, in-flight spinner state, and admin controls.
116: - `App.test.tsx`: Authentication view rendering and form validation.

### Personal Reflection

I used Antigravity with Gemini to help implement the application and ChatGPT to interpret the requirements, prepare development prompts, and independently review the generated code.

The most useful lesson was that passing tests do not automatically mean an implementation is complete. Independent review found gaps in JWT configuration, numeric validation, concurrent registration, and administrator provisioning that the original tests had missed. These findings helped me understand why tests need to challenge failure cases and boundaries, rather than only confirm expected behavior.

AI helped move the project forward quickly, but it also produced confident claims that needed checking against the code and actual results. I used that feedback to request focused fixes and additional regression tests. I also learned to distinguish API integration tests from browser verification and to describe limitations honestly.

For future projects, I would keep the small tests-first workflow, review AI-generated changes earlier, and preserve conversation records throughout development. I take responsibility for understanding the submitted application and explaining both the implementation decisions and the assistance I received.
